title: Let go, i
logline: Monday. The owner says Friday. She says it at the mat cutter, not looking up, which is how she says everything. Wood cuts the mat he was cutting. It's a good mat.

panels.composition: Heceta Frame & Matting, morning. The OWNER at the mat cutter, glasses on a cord. WOOD at the counter. BARNABY in his spot by the radiator.

characters.pose: at the cutter, not looking up

balloons.text: Friday's the last day, Arthur. I'm sorry. It's the rent, not you.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, an older woman with glasses on a cord at a mat cutter not looking up while speaking to a thin man at a frame-shop counter, an old dog by a radiator
image.notes: 'Arthur' — the owner's second of two while he works there (see characters.md).

panels.composition: Wood's hands on the mat he was cutting. Continuing the cut. Straight.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, close-up of a man's hands continuing a straight mat cut with a blade after hearing bad news

panels.composition: The cut done. Wood holding the mat up to the light. Good.

characters.pose: holding a mat to the light

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a thin man holding a cut mat up to a window's light and judging it

panels.composition: The shop. The two of them working. The dog. Four more days of it. The strip doesn't slow down.

notes: 'Friday's the last day, Arthur.' The cut finished straight.
